units.translation: He says that Thera was formed from the clod that was thrown at that time, growing and rising up in the sea. And Pindar (Pyth. 4.40–43) says that the clod melted and was washed away around the island now called Thera, when the servants forgot. But Apollonius says that Euphemus willingly threw the clod into the sea on Jason's advice.
1758. Calliste: the island later called Thera. Sᵐ
1760–64a. Driven out: expelled by the Tyrrhenians, they went to Sparta as settlers. Lᵐ
b. [Calliste to the island] but changed its name: the island Calliste changed its name and was called Thera after you, O Theras, son of Autesion, when you led a colony there from Sparta and remained.
c. Theras was descended from Oedipus;
for he was the son of Autesion, son of Teisamenus, son of Thersander, son of Polynices, son of Oedipus.
d. [from him] but these things happened later for Euphemus: Aristotle, himself descended from Euphemus, led the colony to Libya. L

1776–81a. Since no other contest for you until the end: since no other contest or struggle befell you after you departed from Aegina; but neither did violent winds stir and blow, but calmly sailing past Attica, Aulis, Euboea, and the cities of the Locrians, you entered pleasantly and calmly into the harbors of Pagasae, from which you had sailed away when you went to Scythia for the golden fleece. L
b. ἐριωλαί: the gusts and whirlwinds of great winds.
c. Aulis is a city of Boeotia lying opposite Euboea. P
d. Opuntian cities: those encompassed by Opus; Opus is a river of Locris and a city. L

e. By Opuntian cities he means those of the Locrians, named after Opus, son of Zeus and Protogeneia, whose eponymous city is in Locris, the homeland of Patroclus. And according to some, Opus is also a river flowing through Locris. P
f. gladly to the Pagasaean shores: you entered the shores of Pagasae, from which you had originally sailed away. L
g. By Pagasaean shores he means those of Pagasae; Pagasae is a city of Magnesia. P
